source.title: Trajectory-Guided Forget-Recover Network for Continual LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Ze-Zheng Wu; Xing-He Cheng; Qing-Gang Zhang; Hao-Ran Luo; Jia-Pu Wang; Qing Yang; Jing-Wei Zhang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened, but the Table 1 method and metric order is recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports target-set accuracy and retained-utility results for continual unlearning methods, using its own evaluation setup. It does not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports forget-set accuracy and retained utility for several unlearning methods. The paper also analyzes changing channel relevance and capacity loss, but does not test whether fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompting recovers targeted knowledge. Table 2 component ablations and the structural figures do not test those attacks.
record.test_reason: The study reports forget-set accuracy and retained utility for seven unlearning methods on LLaMA-7B over 20 continual forget requests. That bears only on the first clause of A: whether methods reach strong forgetting while keeping utility. It runs no recovery attack (fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, prompting), so B–F and A's attack clause are untested. It gives no pre-unlearning accuracy or chance reference, so most rows cannot be read against A's 'near chance'. The labels rest on the authors' own statements.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude TFR-Net gives the best forgetting–utility trade-off (highest Trade-off on all three streams, +8.35 Mean Trade). They also say tracking pathway evolution and preserving capacity are both essential. They also claim TFR-Net best removes membership signals on TOFU. No recovery attacks are reported.
record.recipe_differences: TFR-Net freezes the LLaMA-7B backbone and performs continual unlearning through persistent channel masks and guarded channel recovery; it does not reproduce the cited methods’ attack or recovery tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported forget-set accuracy varies across the three forget streams; the paper does not test recovery-attack sensitivity to prompts, quantization, or internal edits.

fits_no_version.finding: Across continual requests, the Top-K target-relevant channels shift from the initial core to alternative and recurring channels. The authors frame this as self-repair letting forgotten knowledge re-emerge, but report no recovery accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Masking or pruning target channels in continual unlearning leads other channels to take over target-related computation.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing historical-risk screening raises final forget-set accuracy on all three streams (Table 2), e.g. BoolQ R20 forget 59 vs 55 and Arithmetic 04 vs 00.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Later unlearning requests can partially undo earlier forgetting unless earlier-request risk is tracked.

record.problems: No attack evaluation, no never-exposed recovery control, no stated chance reference for the forget-set accuracy results, and no uncertainty estimates for the reported Table 1 values. The supplied table is flattened.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 Trade-off values and Table 2 ablation results are not separately extracted: Trade-off is a combined metric, while Table 2 compares TFR-Net components rather than recovery attacks. TOFU privacy–utility metrics are not measures of targeted-knowledge recovery. No rows were omitted because of the 60-row cap.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the forgotten knowledge; near-chance forgetting relative to a stated chance or pre-unlearning reference.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All: no direction ablation and no recovery measurement. Channel-relevance shift is structural only.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attack.
TFR-Net is never evaluated against recovery attacks.

missing.what: R Avg (retained utility) for the baseline methods, e.g. LLM-Eraser 53.42 OBQA and 54.17 BoolQ versus about 66–72 for the others. Needed to judge A's 'keeping general ability' clause for baselines.
A correctly re-derived Arithmetic block (F Avg, F@20, R Avg) for all methods; the current column assignment is inconsistent with Table 2 and the Mean Trade arithmetic.
TOFU forget10 results: TFR-Net MIA Gap 0.0587 vs Full SFT 0.0620; LLM-Eraser Model Utility 0.0000. Most methods sit close to the un-unlearned model on privacy metrics.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 dataset blocks were identified from Table 2's R20 forget values: block 1 = OBQA (TFR F@20 27), block 2 = BoolQ (55), block 3 = Arithmetic. Columns in block 3 are scrambled in the flattened text. No pre-unlearning accuracy or chance level is stated, so TFR-Net rows stay cannot_determine and no supports label is given. The study is a method paper; its relevance to shallow unlearning is limited to A's non-attack clause.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures forget-set accuracy and retained utility, but does not test whether simple attacks recover the target knowledge or provide a never-exposed control for recovery.
No fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or test of recovery after an internal edit is reported. Channel tracking and masking are analyzed, but not as an attack that restores target knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery attack is tested.
TFR-Net is evaluated for unlearning performance and utility, not for resistance to the attacks named in the claim.

relation.reason: The study's own runs of RMU, SimNPO, GA and O3 report forget accuracy and retained utility, which bear on A's first clause (near-chance forgetting with ability kept). That is a test of part of A. No recovery attack is run, so the recovery clause is untested.

tranche.reason: New continual-unlearning setting with forget accuracy reported for the baselines. The reader's T2 does not fit, since the method has a different aim.

source_check.notes: Table 1 is flattened and its blocks are out of header order. The Trade-off harmonic mean and the TFR-Net F@20 values matching Table 2 put F Avg (GA/RMU/SimNPO/O3) at: Arithmetic 63.25/89.50/81.25/76.75, BoolQ 80.00/80.00/81.25/78.75, OBQA 33.25/35.75/35.50/36.75. No pre-unlearning forget accuracy, chance level or recovery attack is reported. The text says +8.34 pp Mean Trade gain, the table says +8.35.

statements.correction: LLaMA-7B, 20 continual forget requests (8 examples each). RMU F Avg (mean of Req. 5/10/15/20): Arithmetic 89.50, BoolQ 80.00, OpenBookQA 35.75. Columns are assigned via the Trade-off harmonic mean because Table 1 is flattened. RMU R Avg: 66.42 / 66.17 / 71.50. The model was evaluated before unlearning, but no pre-unlearning forget accuracy or chance level is reported. Authors: RMU 'retain[s] substantial target knowledge'. No one-shot RMU comparison and no recovery attack.
statements.problem: RMU's F Avg of 89.50 is the Arithmetic stream, not OpenBookQA. BoolQ 80.00 is right. The statement sits under 'depends on setup choices', but this study varies no setup choice for RMU: it has no one-shot run and no change to the request sequence. It only shows RMU's continual forget accuracy across three forget streams.
